newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire gold mine plant believed intact.
newsitem.headline: Zaire gold mine plant believed intact.

text.p: Zairean soldiers looted a major gold mine north of the eastern town of Bunia but the processing plant was believed still intact, a Zairean official said on Thursday.

Regional Commissioner Mbembe Ndoy, who worked for Zaire's government but defected to the rebels when they seized Bunia, told Reuters that workers' homes at Kimin gold mine, 84 km north of Bunia, were looted and equipment was stolen.

"The workers have all fled but the houses have been looted. Clearly a lot of equipment was stolen but we believe the processing plant is intact," said Mbembe, adding his information came from people who had fled the area during the rebel advance.

Mbembe said that Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo-Zaire (ADF) seized the mine from government troops on Saturday. Other Bunia residents confirmed the mine was captured.
The Kimin mine is part of a 2,000 square km concession granted by Okimo (Office des Mines d'Or de Kilo-Moto) to a Canadian-Belgium consortium Mindev.
"The mine was working until very recently and only stopped when expatriate workers were driven off and the retreating soldiers looted the place," said Mbembe.
The Okimo concession covers a total of 83,000 square km in northeast Zaire and reportedly has estimated reserves of at least 100 tonnes of pure gold.
